key_insight: A reconfigurable multimode-fiber optical platform can implement one-way quantum communication complexity and experimentally demonstrate a task with known exponential quantum-classical communication separation.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers a practical photonic hardware route to scalable, reprogrammable quantum communication protocols without increasing hardware complexity.
method: Use multimode fibers with wavefront shaping to build a reconfigurable decoding architecture.
Experimentally implement a genuine one-way quantum communication complexity problem.
Run numerical simulations to test broader tasks and higher-dimensional extensions.
evidence_signal: The paper reports experimental validation of a known communication-complexity task and complementary simulations showing comparable performance on more general one-way protocols.
watch_item: Practical performance may depend on precise wavefront control and the stability/calibration of the multimode-fiber decoding setup.
paper_title: Reconfigurable Optical Platform for One-way Quantum Communication Complexity
